zh: 乘著南太平洋的潮流季風
en: Captain Cook's fleet of sailing ships
Riding the currents and monsoon winds of the South Pacific
The tide rises and falls, the sea shifts, the stars move on
Anecdotes like a painting, legends like a riddle
A modern sail comes into view
From here the music pours forth
Drifting between the jade-green sea and the blue sky

zh: 迴旋於岬灣和岬灣之間
en: The music rises from the sail
Circling between cape and cape, bay and bay
Beauty and dreams take flight with it

zh: 把建築融成如風的音樂
把音樂凝成如帆的建築
en: In the posture of a sail
With the rise and fall of light and shadow at dawn and dusk
With the rhythm of the seasons' colors
Melt architecture into music like the wind
Condense music into architecture like a sail

zh: 美的感動是永恆的喜悅
en: The stirring of beauty is an eternal joy

flow.caption_zh: 清晨薄霧的雪梨歌劇院和雪梨市景。  (攝影/何康隆)

points.zh: 1768年庫克船長 ( Captain James Cook ) 率領船隊奮進號 ( Endeavour ) 自英國出發。1769年10月到達紐西蘭，考察紐西蘭南北二島，并命名南北两島間的海峽為「 Cook Strait 」。後來，紐西蘭最高的山也名為 Aoraki / Mt. Cook。1770年4月19日到達澳州大陸的東南端， 8月21日抵達澳洲最北端，并宣稱澳州為英國佔領地，命名為新威爾士 ( New Wales )。8月23日離開澳州，繼續往太平洋西去。1779年進行第三次航行太平洋時，喪命於夏威夷。庫克船長當年在澳州登陸的地方，現在已開闢為 Botany Bay National Park.
雪梨歌劇院（Sydney Opera House）的建築形態，有如停泊於岬灣上的帆船，展開優雅的白色風帆，乘著習習海風，遨遊於碧波之上。歌劇院是音樂和建築完美結合，妥切的傳達了詩人歌德對音樂和建築的詮釋: “ 音樂是流動的建築，建築是凝佇的音樂“，「Music is liquid architecture，Architecture is frozen music 」。
points.en: The architectural form of the Sydney Opera House resembles a sailing ship moored in a harbor cove, its elegant white sails unfurled, riding the sea breeze as it glides over the blue waves. The Opera House is a perfect union of music and architecture, aptly conveying the poet Goethe's interpretation of music and architecture: "Music is liquid architecture, architecture is frozen music."

points.zh: 雪梨歌劇院是一座世界聞名的建築傑作，其獨特的外型彷彿展開的帆船，漂浮於藍天碧海之間，成為澳洲最具代表性的地標之一。由丹麥建築師約恩·烏松（Jørn Utzon）設計，整體結構融合現代主義與自然意象，展現出動態與詩意的美學。歌劇院的屋頂由多個曲線殼片構成，猶如貝殼或蓮花瓣，在陽光下閃耀如瓷，隨著天色與海光變幻呈現不同風貌，營造出和諧的視覺節奏。其建築不僅技術上創新，更在藝術上引發共鳴，將結構與美感融合得淋漓盡致。內部空間則以木質結構與優雅的幾何設計，營造出溫暖且莊嚴的氛圍，成為音樂與戲劇的殿堂。雪梨歌劇院象徵著人類勇於想像與實踐夢想的精神，其建築之美，超越時代，令人驚嘆不已。2007，雪梨歌劇院成為聯合國教科文組織世界文化遺產。
points.en: The Sydney Opera House is a world-famous architectural masterpiece, its distinctive form resembling unfurled sails, floating between blue sky and sea, making it one of Australia's most iconic landmarks. Designed by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon, its overall structure blends modernist design with natural imagery, displaying a dynamic and poetic aesthetic. The roof is composed of multiple curved shell segments, resembling seashells or lotus petals, gleaming like porcelain in the sunlight and shifting in appearance with the changing sky and sea light, creating a harmonious visual rhythm. The building is not only technically innovative but also artistically resonant, fusing structure and beauty to a remarkable degree. Inside, the wooden structure and elegant geometric design create a warm yet solemn atmosphere, making it a true palace of music and drama. The Sydney Opera House symbolizes humanity's spirit of daring imagination and the pursuit of dreams; the beauty of its architecture transcends its era and continues to astonish. In 2007, the Sydney Opera House was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

points.zh: 「 A thing of beauty is a joy for ever 」 ( 美的事物是永恆的喜悅 ) 是英國詩人濟慈（ John Keats，1795-1821）的詩句。與拜倫、雪萊並稱為浪漫主義第二代詩人。1821濟慈死於旅遊羅馬途中，年僅25。墓碑上沒有他的名字，卻刻著他的遺言: 「Here lies one whose name was written in water」。 一位把名字寫在水上的詩人。
points.en: "A thing of beauty is a joy for ever" (a thing of beauty is an everlasting joy) is a line by the English poet John Keats (1795-1821). Together with Byron and Shelley, he is counted among the second generation of Romantic poets. Keats died in 1821 while traveling in Rome, at only 25 years of age. His tombstone bears no name, but instead carries his own last words: "Here lies one whose name was written in water"—a poet who wrote his name upon water.

points.zh: 詩中列擧歌曲是 " Sydney Philharmonic Choir " 所唱，收錄於 Sydney Opera House 製作的CD  " Ode to Joy:  Great Choral Masterpieces“。
points.en: The song listed in the poem is performed by the Sydney Philharmonic Choir, included on the CD "Ode to Joy: Great Choral Masterpieces," produced by the Sydney Opera House.

points.zh: 參觀 Sydney Opera House 時，歌劇院表演廳寂靜無人，Grace帶領大家合唱鄭智仁醫師的歌曲:“ Formosa 頌“。 廰內歌聲迴盪，飄起濃濃的鄉情，親情和友情。

Formosa 頌  ( 抱着咱的夢 )  詞/鄭瑞堂  曲/鄭智仁
Formosa  咱的夢  咱的愛  親像阿母叫阮的名
摇啊摇啊摇  惜啊惜  永遠抱着美麗的夢
Formosa  咱的夢  咱的愛 有咱祖先流過的汗
摇啊摇啊摇  惜啊惜  永遠抱着美麗的夢
Formosa  咱的夢  咱的愛  無怨無悔來期待
摇啊摇啊摇  惜啊惜  永遠抱着咱的夢

Ode to Formosa (Embracing Our Dream) — Lyrics by Cheng Jui-tang, Music by Cheng Chih-jen
Formosa, our dream, our love, like a mother calling our name
Rocking, rocking, rocking, cherishing, cherishing, forever embracing this beautiful dream
Formosa, our dream, our love, bearing the sweat our ancestors shed
Rocking, rocking, rocking, cherishing, cherishing, forever embracing this beautiful dream
Formosa, our dream, our love, awaited without regret
Rocking, rocking, rocking, cherishing, cherishing, forever embracing our dream

points.zh: 鄭智仁 (1951--, 台湾彰化二水鄉人) ，作詞作曲家和演唱家，是著名的男性生殖醫學專家，獲有多項發明專利，兩度獲選母校中山醫學院傑出校友。2002年以作品「天頂的星」榮獲第13屆金曲獎傳統藝術音樂作品類—「最佳作詞人」及「最佳演唱人」;  同年獲高雄市政府文藝獎—「終身成就獎」。鄭智仁的歌謠，文詞優美、旋律感人，深具本土意識與人文關懷，他的許多作品被收錄在教科書。鄭智仁一直秉持:「音樂家有責任去喚醒伊成長的這塊土地上的靈魂」的信念。 獲選2000 年美國關懷台灣基金會「奉獻獎」，其獲獎的評價是:  鄭智仁是本世紀俱有深遠影響的台灣歌謠作家。
points.en: Cheng Chih-jen (1951– , from Ershui Township, Changhua, Taiwan), lyricist, composer, and singer, is also a renowned specialist in male reproductive medicine, holding multiple invention patents, and has twice been named a Distinguished Alumnus of his alma mater, Chung Shan Medical College. In 2002, his work "The Star in the Sky" won "Best Lyricist" and "Best Vocalist" in the Traditional Arts Music category at the 13th Golden Melody Awards; that same year he received the Kaohsiung City Government's Cultural and Arts Award — Lifetime Achievement Award. Cheng's songs are noted for their beautiful lyrics and moving melodies, deeply imbued with local Taiwanese consciousness and humanistic concern, and many of his works have been included in school textbooks. Cheng has always held to the belief that "a musician has a responsibility to awaken the spirit of the land on which he grew up." He received the American Foundation for Concern about Taiwan's "Dedication Award" in 2000, with the citation describing him as a Taiwanese folk song writer of profound influence in this century.
